body: **2026-10-06-headless-stand** — first measured `disabled="false"` matching `:disabled` on enabled stand buttons and fixed the Dioxus falsy `disabled` write. This matters because the resize dialog's undo/redo and slider rely on the disabled reading staying one way, and the trap still holds: the focus path never had the defect, only state, styling and click targeting did.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — named controls through `aria-label` and `<label>`, gave every Dioxus element its stable id as `author_id`, and wired the Dioxus `accessibility` feature so that the seven_guis stand binary builds no platform adapter (rows `contract/accessibility-tree/author-id`, `decision/dioxus-accessibility-feature-by-name`, `decision/stand-builds-no-platform-adapter`). This is the precedent for naming the canvas «Drawing area» and for keying the `<object>`.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — the snapshot takes role, name and focus from the tree and never from the element, with no second mapping (`decision/snapshot-reads-accessibility-tree`, `decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree`). The canvas's `role="group"` and its name reach the snapshot only through the tree builder.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the actionable-key rule and `unkeyed_actionable` (`decision/actionable-key-rule`). Circle Drawer read 3 unkeyed then. Trap for this chunk: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or a role, because that moves the pinned Tab order. Key the canvas element instead.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — the falsy clear of the bridge's boolean attributes, so `hidden: false` stays in the tree (`decision/falsy-boolean-attribute-removed`, `decision/falsy-boolean-attributes-removed`). It also measured the snapshot's `enabled`, `checked` and `value` from the element (`contract/snapshot/enabled`, `contract/snapshot/value`). The trap it named, that a click on a plain button clears focus, was later reversed.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — `Snapshot::to_text` reads only the snapshot model (`decision/snapshot-model-single-source`, `decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model`). Whatever the canvas states reaches an agent's text only through this one model.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — the changed set's contract and the tree refresh on change. The diff reads the snapshot model, and a text change is reported on the element whose name it changes (`contract/snapshot-diff/entries`). The canvas's `data-circles` attribute write is a mutation that marks the set.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — the stand's expected roles and names are stated once, in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` (`decision/role-name-tables-stated-once`, `decision/stand-expectation-tables`). This is where Circle Drawer's moved rows belong, never in a second mapping.

body: The canvas object's role comes from its role attribute: role group, not the Unknown an object element reads with no role attribute.
The canvas's accessible name «Drawing area», given by an author name attribute on the object, so the actionable canvas carries a name.
Content painted on a canvas crosses only as screenshot pixels: circles and canvas text appear in no snapshot node, accessibility tree node, UI graph node or lint finding.

Engine click synthesis on a custom-widget target: after the widget hears pointer down and up, the engine still queues click and double click, so app click and double-click handlers on the canvas fire; the widget keeps hearing every event; behaviour for every document behind the custom-widget feature, checked in both layout modes.
Double click read on the document's clock and its threshold: two driver clicks on one point with no advance read as a double click, now reaching the canvas object as they did the old div.
A synthetic driver click is a primary click at the node's centre: every driver click on the canvas lands at its centre, a stated limit until drag; no offset argument on click.
A click on the canvas object gives it focus (the object is focusable on click); what the focus and the focus order read with the canvas on screen.
The snapshot's clickable reading and the actionable-node listing for the canvas: it lists as clickable and actionable, keyed by its author id.
Actionable-key rule: every element an agent can act on in Circle Drawer is keyed; unkeyed actionable reads none on its screens (main, resize dialog).
Boot lint clean: the lint on Circle Drawer's boot reads 0 findings in both layout modes, contrast included for the text and controls still on the page.
The resize dialog's diameter slider is a range input: its pointer, key, value and input event behaviour the sample's flow drives through driver calls.
Handler coverage and the reached-handler record: the app's click and double-click handlers on the canvas now reached through the engine's synthesised events.

The driver's element shot of the canvas: a screenshot changes nothing, the element shot shows the painted circles and diameter text from the bundled fonts, and joins the committed cross-OS digest table; the whole screen holds page text and stays outside every cross-OS byte check.

The data-circles attribute: an attribute write on the canvas is a tracked mutation reaching the widget's attribute_changed; malformed text reads as no circle, never a panic; at boot the canvas holds no circle and no text.
The sample's states (circle added, undo, redo, resize dialog open) reached through driver calls in both layout modes, with Circle Drawer's expected rows stated once in the stand's shared tables.
Circle Drawer is not served by the session host and is no lean task: no carrier, count or served list moves.
The snapshot diff and UI graph across a circle added or removed: only DOM-side changes (undo and redo enabled-ness, attribute value not exposed) show, the circles themselves do not.

each new stand screen's expected roles, names, keys and focus order are stated once in the stand's shared tables and asserted from there
each new stand screen reads no lint finding at boot, contrast asserted from computed styles
each new stand check runs in the accessibility test leg and is repeated three rounds

**2026-11-23-canvas-in-a-headless-shot** (Established Decisions: 2 row(s)) — added `+ decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels` (a canvas's app-painted content crosses every ratified carrier only as screenshot pixels, no new verb, field, cause, exit, log field or span; ratified, F1) and `+ decision/harness-paints-custom-widgets` (blitz-test-harness names blitz-paint's custom-widget feature). Why it matters: Circle Drawer's circles move off the DOM onto a widget, so they leave the snapshot, tree, graph and lint and reach an agent only as shot pixels; the scope's "no new verb, carrier or field" boundary rests on this row, and the stand checks' shot of the circles relies on the harness feature.

Why it matters: the chunk states the widget's paint, placement and pointer frame stand as built, so the circle drawing and the forwarded pointer coordinates read in that content-box frame; the new click synthesis must keep the widget hearing every pointer event as that ruling made it.

Why it matters: Circle Drawer's canvas text (each circle's diameter at its centre) is painted from the document's own font context through `Widget::fonts`, as scope F3 A and matrix#v040-09 require, with no new font path.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (`CustomWidget`'s attribute replay) — `ElementData::set_custom_widget` replays each existing attribute to `Widget::attribute_changed` with no old value, behind `custom-widget` (upstream #1322, `a26c6ddeb`). Why it matters: the circle list reaches the widget as one `data-circles` attribute parsed in `attribute_changed`; the replay means the widget sees the attribute already set at mount, and the parser must take a missing old value and malformed text as no circle without a panic.

**2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts** (Existing Scopes: 1 row(s), amd-bs66iouj) — `~ decision/no-screenshot-in-cross-os-byte-check` except: a canvas-only shot is held byte-equal on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 by one committed digest table, no pixels committed; a shot holding document text stays out (F1 A). Why it matters: Circle Drawer's element shot of its canvas joins `stand_canvas_cross_os`'s digest table under this exception. If the canvas paints diameter text, that shot holds text drawn from the bundled font, so the watch's cross-OS equality must be measured. The whole screen stays outside every cross-OS byte check.

**2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts** (Existing Scopes: 1 row(s), amd-pbnf5rg7) — the same row's why restated: a shot holding document text differs in PNG bytes between linux and macOS, and a canvas-only shot reads equal on the three hosts. Why it matters: this is the measured cause behind the digest table this chunk extends. A canvas shot whose diameter text comes from the bundled font is a case between those two readings, so it is the chunk's to measure on CI before its digest is committed.

body: The engine's click synthesis on a custom-widget target: after the widget hears a pointer press and release, the engine still queues the click and double-click events, so app handlers fire; the widget still hears every event; the change sits in a function of the fork's own and reaches every document behind the custom-widget feature, checked by a new engine check in both layout modes.

The synthesised click and double click on a canvas follow the engine's existing click rules: a cancelled pointer release still clicks, the event's trusted flag is set by its dispatch source, and the focus the canvas object takes on a click stays as it is.

Canvas content crosses only as screenshot pixels: the circles and their painted diameter text leave the snapshot, the accessibility tree, the UI graph and the lint, and no carrier gains a field for them.

The data-circles attribute is markup attribute text read by the widget's attribute-changed reader: malformed or hostile text reads as no circle, with no panic and no log line; its text leaves only by the ratified carriers and never in a driver reply.

The widget's attribute replay and paint path as earlier canvas chunks built them: the initial attribute is replayed to the widget, an attribute write is a tracked mutation that reaches the widget, paint and pointer frame sit in the element's content box.
Canvas text drawn from the document's own font context handed to the widget, from the bundled fonts; no font source taken from page or agent input.
The canvas's accessible role group and its name Drawing area: the name exits only by the ratified carriers of accessible names and is kept out of logs.

Every element an agent can act on in Circle Drawer is keyed, so each carries a stable element id from its author key; the unkeyed-actionable reading is none on its screens under the one actionable rule.
Boot lint on Circle Drawer reads 0 findings in both layout modes; lint findings hold no page content.

A driver click on the canvas lands at the element's centre through the shared target check; two clicks there with no advance read as a double click; no offset argument, no new verb, carrier, served task or field joins the closed driver verb schema.

The resize dialog's diameter slider is a range input: its pointer and key actions, its sanitised finite on-grid value and where its current value exits stand as they are and are reached by the flow checks.
Circle Drawer is booted in process by the stand only: the session host's served task list, its socket grammar and its replies do not move.
Circle Drawer's canvas element shot joins the committed cross-OS digest table; its whole screen holds page text and stays outside every cross-OS byte check; shots are PNG-encoded and carried in band.

The sample's manifest takes the widget's crates at workspace-inherited versions, no git dependency, under locked builds; Dioxus stays at 0.7.3; the harness keeps the paint crate's custom-widget feature on.
The capability statement names the canvas sample and its stated limit, with no served-task count moving.
